To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the malignant haematopoietie cell lines can be classified into lymphoma, myeloma and leukemia lines, and that the lymphoma lines can be classified further into non-Burkett lymphoma lines, Burkitt lymphoma and lymphoblastoid lines, the latter being EBV carrying lines derived from normal B-lymphocytes.
the malignant cell lines of B-cell origin have all the surface markers of normal B cells, whereas the myeloma cell lines lack Fc and complement receptors.
the lymphoid cell line U-698 M, which has been derived from a non-Burkett lymphoma, has only trace amounts of immunoglobulins on its surface.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of surface receptors on human haemopoietic cell line.

the characterization of surface receptors of malignant human haematopoetic cells and the results obtained may be of value to the identification of cell lines of haematopoietical origin and of their derivation from normal cells.
the characterization of the surface receptors on human haemopoietic cell line of proved malignant derivation, with the aim of establishing a pattern of markers for the discrimination of these lines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the surface receptors of the malignant haematopoietics cells are not identical with those of the normal counterparts.
the expression of complement, Fc and SRBC receptors is not restricted to B-lymphocytes, but that it may be found in a variety of malignant and non-malignant haematopoietietic cell lines.
the surface markers studied here are not of diagnostic value for the differentiation between lymphoid, myeloma and leukaemia lines.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the expression of B-lymphotypic markers on human haematopoitic cell lines of malignant origin is related to the origin of the cell lines and that the expression of surface immunoglobulin on these lines is not a constant feature.
the lymphoid cell surface phenotype is not a constant property of the malignant lymphoid cell.
malignant cells of lymphoid origin may be identified as B-lymphocytes by the presence of C3 receptors and/or surface immunoglobuline.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of surface immunoglobulin is a reliable marker of B-lymohocyte origin in malignant cell lines.
the expression of B-lyphocyte surface markers on malignant haematopoieti cells is not necessarily related to their malignant origin.
malignant cells may be distinguished from non-malignant ones by the expression of B-lyphocyte markers.
